freshness_policy.rule: Review the Artificial Analysis release feed daily and re-verify provider pricing/specifications at least weekly. Price, context and Intelligence Index require explicit sources. Previously charted rows may retain price/intelligence comparisons when speed and TTFT become explicitly unavailable on both model and provider pages, recorded as null with dated provenance. Never infer absence from a parser failure, rank unavailable performance or reuse historical samples as current evidence.

reviewed_not_charted.reason: Reflection documents a public-beta API, but no standard first-party USD-per-token tariff was established in the reviewed launch and API documentation. Artificial Analysis lists four measured third-party providers and no Reflection provider row. Retain outside the chart until first-party pricing and matching provider performance are verified; free-to-start access is not a standard paid API quote.

Meta explicitly states that Muse Spark Open is not called over Meta Model API; users self-host its weights or use hosted inference providers. Artificial Analysis lists five third-party providers and no Meta provider row. Official Model API tariffs for Muse Spark 1.3/1.2/1.1 must not be reused for Open. Retain outside the first-party API chart until a comparable source-matched API row exists.

NVIDIA documents open weights and local deployment. Artificial Analysis explicitly lists zero API providers, with hosted API pricing, output speed and latency unavailable. A sourced per-request API comparison cannot be constructed; local hardware throughput does not supply the missing hosted API metrics.

NVIDIA documents open weights, NIM and self-hosted deployment. Artificial Analysis supplies pricing and performance through seven external providers but no NVIDIA first-party provider row. No NVIDIA standard USD-per-token tariff paired with a measured NVIDIA API endpoint was established in the reviewed primary sources. Retain outside the first-party API chart rather than relabel third-party prices or performance.

Meta released Muse Wonder Full on 2026-10-12 for Muse Code Power/Maximum subscription only: NOT available through the per-token Model API, so cost per API request is not comparable. Artificial Analysis scores it 56 but reports no public API provider or token prices. Sources: https://dev.meta.ai/docs/models ; https://dev.meta.ai/resources/blog/build-with-muse-wonder ; https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/muse-wonder-full .

Meta released Muse Wonder on 2026-10-12 with official Model API pricing $4 input/$20 output per MTok, 1,048,576 context and Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 52. Held out of the comparable current chart until source-matched output speed and TTFT for the first-party API are both verified (new release and provider performance observations are still changing). Exact model is muse-wonder-1.0; do not substitute Muse Wonder Full. Sources: https://dev.meta.ai/models/muse-wonder ; https://dev.meta.ai/docs/pricing-rate-limits ; https://artificialanalysis.ai/models/muse-wonder .

methodology.benchmark: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5.0.1. Performance v3 reports end-to-end speed and first-answer latency, which are incompatible with the legacy speed and TTFT fields; these remain unavailable rather than relabelled.
methodology.pricing: Use first-party standard API list prices in USD when the provider publishes them directly. Where a provider's public documentation does not expose a stable USD table, use Artificial Analysis's explicitly reported price for that model's first-party API and label that fallback in the source note. Tool/search/grounding charges, cache writes, volume discounts, batch pricing and premium service tiers are excluded. Announced future prices are encoded when available.
methodology.workload: Scenario cost uses editable input and output token counts: cost = input_tokens × input_rate / 1e6 + output_tokens × output_rate / 1e6. It does not estimate hidden reasoning-token usage unless the provider bills those tokens as output and they are present in the supplied output-token count.
methodology.frontier: A model is on the displayed price/intelligence frontier when no other scored model has both an equal-or-higher Intelligence Index and an equal-or-lower scenario cost, with at least one strict improvement.
methodology.comparability: Performance v3 reports different quantities; legacy post-start output speed and first-token latency are unavailable unless the exact original quantities are independently established on the model and provider pages. Release coverage is broader than the chart.
